What it means inside Osprey: The precursors (targets + paired decoys) of every protein with 2+ distinct detected peptides in the first pass; only these get new q-values in the second pass, the rest keep their first-pass q.
Proposed replacement: state the effect: 'q-values are recomputed only for precursors of proteins with 2+ detected peptides; all others keep their first-pass q-values'
Brendan decision so far: This seems like a very long explanation. I also think "protein-compact" is vague. The "compact" part is reducing the set to precursor candidates with per-run q value (under consideration) < 0.01, and then in fact enhancing the choices by adding back precursor candidates for proteins with >= peptides that passed this filter. But "protein-compact" is currently an argument term for the software. So "protein-compact subset" may simply convey the subset considered under this flag. Or "precursor candidate set with >= 2 detections per protein", "detections" is a well used general term that indicates passing some cut-off without indicating exactly what that cut-off is. Currently is it run-level q value < 1% which has issues, but that is what is counted as a "detection" at this stage.
